name: frontier-census
written_before: any of the new rows was planned; the 94 existing plans are cached and untouched
kind: corpus widening, no compiler change — semantics version HELD at 6
claim_under_test: The census thesis: checkpoint count grows quickly, family-generation count more slowly, semantic-idea count slowest. The taxonomy is CLOSED to new clusters without code, so every blocker on a new row lands either in an existing cluster (vocabulary reuse) or in `unclustered` (vocabulary gap). The split is the measurement.
The two doors hold on checkpoints nobody wrote code for: BUG stays 0 and no new row passes the gate while carrying an unread declaration.

result.attention_schedule_reach: 16 -> 23 whole-model; text closure 23 (predicted >= 9 gain: got 7 whole-model — Command A+ and EXAONE-4.0 consumed layer_types/sliding_window, which the forecast did not credit)
result.verdict: EXACT on every outcome, including the two negatives (Mistral Large 3 no config.json, Command A gated) and the one AMBER (Hy4-preview). Cluster-membership predictions were coarser: 14 of 21 planned rows matched the predicted cluster set exactly, 7 carried extra generic clusters (ffn_activation, norm_geometry, execution_surface, attention_bias) that follow from an unregistered family rather than from any key the forecast reasoned about.
findings: Hy4-preview is AMBER because its indexer and hyper-connection leaves match the unsupported-component table — and the component labels read '(GLM-5.x)' on a Tencent checkpoint. The table is leaf-keyed but family-labelled. `indexer_types` is named as a component yet reports cluster `unclustered`: named in one table, absent from the other.

EXAONE-4.0-1.2B blocks on exactly 4 subjects — architecture_family, target.execution_surface, hidden_act, rms_norm_eps — none of which is a config fact the model declares unusually. Its `sliding_window: null` + `sliding_window_pattern: null` + all-full layer_types passed as inert (wave 6's companion gate reached a third spelling). Everything left is the unregistered family. Registering exaone4 is NOT a Llama alias: EXAONE 4 uses QK-Reorder-Norm, so the family entry must declare that.

Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B blocks on 3 (hidden_act, num_experts_per_tok, shared_expert_intermediate_size). At the TOP level `rope_parameters.partial_rotary_factor` did not block; nested under text_config on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B it does. Same key, two fates by nesting — see per-key check below.

Command A+ declares layer_types sliding/full with sliding_window 4096 and attention_schedule is NOT in its text closure: the schedule is consumed generically. Step-3.5 declares the same shape and attention_schedule IS in its closure — its `use_rope_layers`, `yarn_only_types`, `partial_rotary_factors` (plural) and sliding_window 512 co-declare, so the blocker is the per-layer rope schedule spelled beside it, not the window.

Nemotron 3 Ultra and 3.5 Lightning spell the hybrid schedule as `layers_block_type` (a list, no num_hidden_layers) where Nano and Super spell it `hybrid_override_pattern` (a string). One family, two dialects, same generation year. LFM2 likewise: 350M uses full_attn_idxs, 2.6B uses layer_types.
Mistral Large 3 ships params.json only, in every variant. The sweep reports it as absent; the honest reason is a config DIALECT the source does not read, and the script now says so.
